assertion: Two E. coli strains (BL21(DE3) and K-12) and two Klebsiella species (K. pneumoniae and K. aerogenes KCTC 2190) account for 40.24% of all duodenal bacteria in SIBO subjects (≥10³ CFU/mL on MAC) vs 5.6% in non-SIBO subjects. Shotgun sequencing (n=38) confirmed these specific strains. The E. coli strains were hardly detectable in non-SIBO duodenum. Enterobacteriaceae RA was increased in SIBO subjects (log₂ FC 2.43, adjusted P=2.66E-7).

qualifiers.magnitude: 40.24% of duodenal bacteria in SIBO vs 5.6% in non-SIBO; Enterobacteriaceae log₂ FC=2.43 (adjusted P=2.66E-7); E. coli FC=6.55 (P=4.8E-4), K. pneumoniae FC=12.43 (P=9.4E-12), K. aerogenes FC=24.76 (P=4.3E-11), Enterobacter FC=22.11 (P=7.1E-8)
qualifiers.conditions: duodenal aspirate via double-lumen sterile catheter; 16S rRNA (n=483 with culture) confirmed by shotgun metagenomics (n=38)
qualifiers.population: 505 adults undergoing EGD; 385 non-SIBO (<10³ CFU/mL), 98 SIBO (≥10³ CFU/mL) on MAC

provenance.ref: Leite et al. Defining Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth by Culture and High Throughput Sequencing
provenance.location: Results — Specific Coliform Strains section, p.266; Discussion p.268
provenance.original_text: Duodenal RA of specific Enterobacteriaceae species were increased in subjects with ≥10³ CFU/mL vs those with <10³ CFU/mL, including Escherichia coli (FC, 6.55; adjusted P = 4.8E-4), Klebsiella pneumoniae (FC, 12.43; adjusted P = 9.4E-12), Klebsiella aerogenes (FC, 24.76; adjusted P = 4.3E-11)... This remarkably specific group of microbes account for 40.24% of duodenal bacteria in SIBO subjects, compared with 5.6% in non-SIBO subjects.

integrity.coi_detail: Pimentel lab (Cedars-Sinai MAST). Study funded by institutional funds. Pimentel has consulting relationships with multiple GI pharma companies.

chain_hints: CRITICAL BIO: First strain-level identification of SIBO-dominant organisms in a large cohort
Only 4 strains/species account for majority of overgrowth — remarkably specific
E. coli BL21(DE3) and K-12 were hardly detectable in non-SIBO — these are not commensals drifting upward but true invaders
Connects to SYM-009 (strain-symptom correlations from same study)
Connects to MECH-023/024 (metabolic pathways enriched by these organisms)
